item.title: Europe gripped by cost-of-living turmoil
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-23
Europe gripped by cost-of-living turmoil People throughout the continent take to the streets to protest against rising prices, reduced purchasing power The wave of protests and unrest that swept through France and several other European countries in recent days may soon subside, but the economic pressure and widespread frustration that caused it remain. For Laurent Mazzarolo, a train driver living in Paris, the demonstrations reflect the growing difficulty ordinary people face in maintaining their living standards, as prices rise and purchasing power weakens. "Ten years ago, you could live quite comfortably on a salary of 2,000 euros ($2,247) a month. Now, even with 3,000 euros, life can be quite difficult, especially in Paris," he said. "Before, you could go to a restaurant four or five times a month. Now, maybe once or twice, or sometimes not at all. People have less money to enjoy themselves, and that means less social interaction," he said. Even with a stable job, Mazzarolo said he struggles to balance his monthly expenses, despite cutting back on leisure spending, and that makes him particularly concerned about people in younger generations, who face difficulties in securing a place at their preferred university and in pursuing the careers they want. "They cannot imagine their future," he said. "I can understand why people are frustrated about the cost of living, but I don't like the way it's being expressed through violence. For me, that's not the right way." Similar concerns are being voiced in Madrid, where the rising cost of housing has left young people worried about the prospect of living independently. Rocio, an 18-year-old student who lives with her parents and brother, said she joined a protest because she fears she may eventually be unable to afford a home of her own. "The prices just keep on getting higher, and I know by the time I can live on my own, they will be even higher," she said. Richard, a Frenchman living in Brussels, Belgium, has similar fears. "Today, when I go to (the supermarket) to buy three items, say a pack of milk and some cereal, I pay 15 euros," he said. "If you're a parent, the question arises: how can you teach your children that quality matters, and what values are you truly able to pass on? Ultimately, for someone like me in a comfortable income bracket, the question comes down to one word: dignity. Can you live with dignity when you work? That is, can your work enable you to pay your bills and provide for your children's needs, while still looking at life with some sense of hope, rather than being driven solely by day-to-day necessity?" Economic indicators illustrate the situation. According to Eurostat data, annual inflation in the area that uses the euro for currency rose to 3.8 percent in September, after having been 3.2 percent in August. Energy prices increased in September by 18.8 percent year-on-year, after having been 14.3 percent the previous month. The high cost of energy is widely believed to add disproportionate pressure to lower-income households, leaving them less money for food, healthcare, education, and housing. Rising rent According to Deutsche Bank Research Institute's report Mapping the World's Prices 2026, a household with two earners receiving average local net salaries in Lisbon, Portugal, would have just 253 euros left each month after renting a three-bedroom apartment in the city center, which is the smallest amount of disposable income recorded among 28 European cities surveyed. The pressure is also evident in Brussels, where the average monthly rent for newly signed leases through real estate agencies rose from 1,113 euros in 2021 to 1,376 euros in 2025, according to the CIB-Korfine Rental Barometer. That represents an increase of approximately 23.6 percent in four years, adding 263 euros to the average monthly rental bill for newly contracted properties. Yan Xiaoxiao, an associate researcher at the Institute of International Relations at the Shanghai Academy of Social Sciences, who is conducting research in Europe, said the protests across the continent point to a common economic dilemma. "With economic growth slowing, governments are finding it increasingly difficult to meet public expectations for living standards and social protection," he said. "On the one hand, people expect governments to improve public services and provide more public goods to ease the pressure on their daily lives. On the other hand, governments are under pressure to reduce fiscal deficits." Yan noted that the current wave of protests has involved people from different age groups and occupations, reflecting discontent that extends beyond any single section of society. Past protests have tended to attract participants from specific sections of society. "The latest unrest can be seen as an expression of dissatisfaction that has accumulated since its last breakout," he said. "I paid 18.50 euros for a tube of eye ointment and 11.50 euros for a simple meal at McDonald's," Yan said. "I can't imagine my financial pressure if I were to live here for a long time." Li Zhengdong, an associate professor at the Institute of Central and Eastern European Studies at Ningbo University, who is on an academic tour in Europe, noted: "The real test facing Europe today is not simply whether governments can contain street violence, but whether they can prevent mounting socioeconomic tensions from escalating into divisions between different social groups and, ultimately, a political crisis." Back in Paris, Mazzarolo said he suspects "the government is doing what it can, but not enough". He said policymakers should strive to be "closer to the people" and "act like normal people". "Sometimes, we have the feeling that politicians are living on another planet," he said. "Even if you don't have the solutions, at least show more empathy." Asked what he expects the government to do after the protests end, 22-year-old Jorge Salas in Madrid replied: "Right now, nothing. For years, we haven't received a real answer or any meaningful help. The demonstrations are about more than housing costs. They also reflect concerns over education, access to public services, and the opportunities available to ordinary people." Salas pointed to the financial burden the purchase of schoolbooks places on low-income families, saying that providing children with a good education should be a government priority. "We need books, we need food, we need help to buy a house and start a family," he said. "We are not simply asking for a better life. We are asking for a chance to improve our lives." Huang Xiaodi contributed to the story. Contact the writers at zhangzhouxiang@chinadaily.com.cn.

item.title: RMB going global serves real economy
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-23
RMB going global serves real economy Quality of yuan's cross-border and worldwide use is steadily improving The internationalization of the renminbi is following a steady path that responds to market demand. Its foundation lies in serving the real economy, while its primary driving force is determined by market choices and forces, said an official of China's central bank. Speaking at the Global RMB Forum during the Annual Conference of Financial Street Forum 2026, held in Beijing on Wednesday, Xi Yu, deputy director-general of the macroprudential policy bureau of the People's Bank of China, said as the international monetary system has become more diversified in recent years, an increasing number of businesses have chosen to use the RMB, also known as the yuan, for cross-border settlements. Chinese banks operating in the country — along with numerous foreign banks and financial groups — have been actively responding to this market demand by developing more use cases for the RMB and expanding their financial services. "The use of the RMB has evolved from its initial applications in merchandise trade settlement, trade financing and direct investment to a broader range of areas, including financing across multiple sectors, securities investment and asset management. Both the quality and efficiency of the RMB's cross-border and international use are steadily improving," Xi said. The 2026 White Paper on the Global Use of RMB, unveiled by Bank of China, said the total value of cross-border RMB settlement in China was approximately 70.6 trillion yuan ($10.58 trillion) in 2025, up 10.2 percent year-on-year. Lu Lei, deputy governor of the PBOC, said on Sept 10 that overseas entities currently hold more than 11 trillion yuan in onshore RMB financial assets, and the cumulative issuance of panda bonds has exceeded 1.3 trillion yuan. Looking ahead, Zhang Hui, president of Bank of China, said international use of the Chinese currency has substantial room for growth. China's development is injecting greater stability and certainty into the world economy while enhancing the attractiveness of RMB-denominated assets. "As a virtuous cycle of borrowing, using and investing in the renminbi gathers pace worldwide, the currency is increasingly becoming a preferred choice for users around the globe seeking to improve payment efficiency, enhance investment returns and manage risks effectively," Zhang said. During the process, Hong Kong plays an important role in RMB clearing, financing and investment, and risk management. Currently, more than 75 percent of global offshore RMB payments are processed through Hong Kong. As of end-July, the outstanding balance of RMB deposits and certificates of deposit in Hong Kong had reached approximately 1.3 trillion yuan, making it the world's largest offshore RMB liquidity pool. Last year, offshore RMB lending in Hong Kong hit a record high of 935 billion yuan, said Michael Wong Wai-lun, deputy financial secretary of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. The Hong Kong SAR government is actively advancing a range of measures to expand the offshore RMB market and make it deeper and more stable. To enhance offshore RMB liquidity, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority has increased the size of its RMB Business Facility to 500 billion yuan and extended the loan tenor to up to three years, Wong said. In addition, Hong Kong is promoting the issuance of a wider variety of offshore RMB products and will further improve the offshore RMB yield curve, he said. RMB business is also an important part of the broader UK-China financial relationship. According to this year's London RMB business annual report, the total cumulative RMB clearing volume in London reached 48.15 trillion yuan in 2025, and the average daily clearing volume increased by 55.33 percent to 191.09 billion yuan.

item.title: Diplomats explore Beijing culture, tech in Shijingshan
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-23
The "2026 Chinese Cultural Tour for Consular Officials of Foreign Embassies in China" was held in the Shijingshan district of Beijing on Monday. More than 60 diplomats and representatives of cultural and tourism institutions from over 30 countries and regions took part under the theme "Wow! Shijingshan: Culture & Tourism, Reimagined". They traced the district's rich cultural heritage through ancient art at Fahai Temple, explored technological innovation through human-robot interaction at the Humanoid Robot Data Training Center, and witnessed urban transformation along the Yongding River. The event was hosted by the Bureau of International Exchange and Cooperation of the Ministry of Culture and Tourism, and organized by the culture and tourism bureau of Shijingshan district and China Tourism Group Travel Services Co Ltd.

item.title: 16 killed, 76 injured after 7.0-magnitude quake hits Xizang
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-23
President Xi Jinping has ordered all-out search and rescue efforts for the missing and prompt medical treatment for the injured after the earthquake. Sixteen people were killed and 76 others injured after the earthquake. Electricity and communications have been restored in some villages in the hardest-hit areas of Drachen county. China's transport authorities have stepped up road inspections and emergency support to ensure rescue vehicles can reach areas affected by a magnitude-7.0 earthquake in Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region. Roads in the quake-hit area are under traffic controls, with access maintained for rescue vehicles while other vehicles are temporarily barred, according to the Ministry of Transport. The earthquake struck Drachen county in Nagchu at 10:33 pm on Thursday. By 10 am Friday, 16 people had been killed and 76 injured, according to local authorities. The ministry activated a Level III emergency response for road transport at 9 am Friday and dispatched a team to coordinate rescue support and efforts to keep roads open. It is also coordinating with the Ministry of Finance to arrange emergency funding for road clearance and repairs. Level III is the second-lowest level in the ministry's four-tier response system, with Level I being the highest. Xizang's transport department activated its own Level II response after the earthquake. Local highway authorities deployed 178 personnel and 39 pieces of machinery to inspect affected sections of five national highways and seven provincial roads. They have checked 2,377 kilometers of roads, 295 bridges and 635 culverts. The inspections found varying degrees of damage along sections of national highway G345 and provincial highway S301. More detailed inspections of roads, bridges and other transport infrastructure are continuing. Emergency equipment is being sent to the disaster-hit area from reserve centers in Lhasa and Qamdo to help crews clear debris and repair roads. Crews from nearby construction projects run by centrally administered State-owned enterprises, along with other road maintenance teams, are on standby to provide additional support. Electricity and communications have been restored in some villages in the hardest-hit areas of Drachen county, Xizang autonomous region, following a magnitude-7.0 earthquake on Thursday, according to the Xizang Communications Administration. State Grid Xizang Electric Power activated its emergency response and dispatched teams overnight to Gangche and Maru townships to inspect and secure power facilities. Electricity has been restored across the area surrounding the Maru township government offices. Phone and internet services have also returned to normal in two villages in the township. Being close to the earthquake's epicenter, they were among the most affected areas. According to the administration, the earthquake knocked 628 mobile base stations offline, accounting for 8.5 percent of the city's total. These stations have been restored as of 10:30 am Friday, bringing communications in the affected area back to pre-earthquake levels within 12 hours. The administration said 131 emergency repair personnel and 50 vehicles had been deployed to restore communications, along with 38 generators and other emergency equipment. Telecommunications networks in the disaster area are now operating normally, supporting the coordination of rescue operations. Earthquake authorities in Yunnan and Sichuan provinces have sent a dozen personnel to the affected area to assess the quake's intensity, verify damage, and conduct other emergency field operations. Sixteen people have been killed and 76 injured as of 1 pm Friday following Thursday's magnitude-7.0 earthquake in Drachen county, Xizang autonomous region, officials said at a news conference Friday. Dondrub, mayor of Nagchu city, which administers the county, said rescuers had completed three rounds of searches, checking key areas and visiting residents in remote, scattered settlements. Authorities have set up 18 temporary shelters and relocated 12,489 people, he said. Due to the quake, 339 households have collapsed or been damaged, along with 20 livestock sheds. The immediate priorities are treating the injured and ensuring displaced residents have access to basic necessities, he said. Authorities will provide insulated tents and hot meals, with particular attention to older people, children, pregnant women, new mothers, and people with disabilities. Rescuers went door to door in villages near the epicenter of a magnitude-7.0 earthquake that struck Drachen county, Xizang autonomous region, looking for anyone in need of help. In Gangche township, one of the areas closest to the epicenter, rescue workers began searching for people trapped in their homes in the early hours of Friday morning. Surveillance footage shared by local media showed buildings shaking violently, with goods tumbling from shelves as residents rushed outside to escape the quake on Thursday night. In Maru township, one of the hardest-hit areas, the earthquake cracked the ground and caused sections of road to sink, China Central Television reported. "Suddenly, there was a tremendous rumbling. For a moment, it felt as if hundreds of yaks were running at once," said Dzondru Tseltrim, a resident of Garuthang village in the county. His family had already gone to bed when the shaking began. Woken by the tremors, he heard cabinets and wooden pillars creaking inside the house. He rushed to wake his father, in his 80s, and helped him outside. Other family members soon followed. Fearing aftershocks, the family decided not to sleep indoors that night. They arranged for his father to rest in a car while the others prepared to spend the night in the courtyard. BEIJING -- China has allocated 50 million yuan (about $7.5 million) in emergency disaster relief funds and earmarked another 30 million yuan for recovery efforts following a 7.0-magnitude earthquake in Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region. The earthquake struck Drachen county of the city of Nagchu at 10:33 pm on Thursday, leaving 16 people dead and 65 injured. The Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Emergency Management jointly allocated 50 million yuan to support rescue operations and assistance to affected residents, while the National Development and Reform Commission earmarked the additional 30 million yuan from the central budget to help restore damaged infrastructure and public service facilities. The country has also upgraded its national earthquake emergency response from Level IV to Level III, while activating a separate Level IV national natural disaster relief response. China's national comprehensive fire and rescue force has dispatched a total of 350 rescuers and 83 vehicles for rescue operations. The emergency management ministry has guided Xizang's emergency management department in arranging for Wing Loong drone deployment to the quake-hit area for disaster reconnaissance. As of 6:30 am on Friday, 120 rescuers and 27 vehicles had arrived in the quake-hit area, while the remaining 230 rescuers and 56 vehicles from the Xizang fire and rescue corps were en route as reinforcements, having all entered Nagqu's administrative area. Earlier, as of 4:30 am on Friday, authorities had mobilized relief supplies at the central, regional, municipal and county levels, and delivered them in batches to the affected area. These supplies included 1,000 prefabricated housing units, 3,239 tents, 2,821 folding beds and 4,280 quilts, among other essentials. The number of people injured in the 7.0-magnitude earthquake that struck Drachen county in Nagchu city, Xizang autonomous region, has risen to 65, including 11 seriously injured and 54 with minor injuries, according to the city's earthquake relief headquarters. As of 10 am Friday, rescue teams had safely evacuated 12,489 residents from affected areas. Search and rescue operations, damage assessments, and efforts to provide temporary shelter for displaced residents are ongoing. By early Friday, rescue teams and relief supplies reached earthquake-hit Drachen county in Nagchu, Xizang autonomous region, as authorities upgraded the national earthquake emergency response to Level III, the third highest of the four-tier system, the Ministry of Emergency Management said on Friday. A 7.0-magnitude earthquake struck the county at 10:33 pm on Thursday, killing 16 people and injuring 54. A working team from the central government has been dispatched to the disaster area to guide and assist relief efforts. The ministry has guided the Xizang autonomous region's emergency management department to send Wing Loong drones to the disaster area to assess the damage. By 4:30 am on Friday, relief supplies allocated by authorities at the central, autonomous region, city, and county levels had arrived in the disaster area. The relief supplies comprised of 1,000 prefabricated housing units, about 3,200 tents, about 2,800 folding beds, and 100 mattresses, along with quilts, stoves, cotton clothing, overcoats, and Tibetan robes. Also included were four generators, 1,000 hand-crank solar flashlights, and 1,000 head-mounted outdoor lights. By 6:30 am on Friday, 120 personnel and 27 vehicles had arrived in the disaster area. Another 230 personnel and 56 vehicles from the Xizang Fire and Rescue Corps were en route, having reached Nagchu. The Red Cross Society of China has activated an emergency response on Friday, allocating 3,800 sets of relief supplies, including hygiene kits, heating stoves, cotton tents, windproof jackets, folding beds, and cotton quilts. It has also dispatched a working group to the disaster zones to guide local efforts in relocating affected residents. China's Ministry of Natural Resources activated a Level III geological disaster emergency response for the Xizang autonomous region at 6 am on Friday, after a magnitude-7.0 earthquake struck the region on Thursday evening. According to the China Earthquake Networks Center, the quake hit Drachen county of Nagchu city in Xizang at 10:33 pm on Thursday, with a focal depth of 10 kilometers. So far, at the time of publication, it has resulted in 16 deaths and 54 injuries. Under the third-highest level emergency response in the four-tier system, an expert working group has been dispatched by the ministry to the quake-hit area to assist with emergency technical support, secondary geological hazard screening, and on-site disposal. The ministry required the Xizang natural resources department to carry out immediate patrols and investigations, strengthen monitoring and early warning, conduct joint risk assessments, handle disaster reports, and maintain 24-hour duty with timely information reporting. The China Geological Survey and the ministry's technical guidance center for geological disasters were tasked with coordinating expert deployments and enhancing assessment and scheduling to support local disaster prevention efforts. Rescue teams are continuing search and rescue operations on Friday after a 7.0-magnitude earthquake struck Drachen county in Nagchu city, Xizang autonomous region, killing 16 people and injuring 65 others. As of 10 am on Friday, 11 people were seriously injured and 54 sustained minor injuries, the city's earthquake relief headquarters said, Xinhua News Agency reported. A total of 339 households had homes collapsed or were damaged, while 20 livestock enclosures were damaged. The earthquake struck at 10:33 pm Thursday at a depth of 10 kilometers, according to the China Earthquake Networks Center. Firefighters rescued a trapped resident from a village at around 2:20 am Friday, CCTV reported. Rescue personnel were also conducting searches and damage assessments in other affected villages. Xizang's fire and rescue authorities mobilized 347 rescuers and 82 vehicles, along with more than 4,200 pieces of rescue equipment. More than 300 police officers were also dispatched to the hardest-hit areas, according to Xinhua. Emergency supplies dispatched by authorities at national, regional, municipal, and county levels began arriving in the disaster zone by 4:30 am, including 1,000 prefabricated housing units, 3,239 tents, 2,821 folding beds, 4,280 quilts, and winter clothing. Xizang has activated a Level III emergency response for disaster relief, while national authorities have upgraded their Level IV response to Level III and dispatched working groups to assist local rescue and relief operations. The Nagchu meteorological observatory warned that intermittent snow showers and strong winds could affect the earthquake-hit area over the next three days, with snow accumulation and icy roads posing additional risks to rescue and transport operations. A magnitude-7 earthquake struck Drachen county of Nagchu city, Xizang autonomous region at 10:33 pm on Thursday, with a focal depth of 10 kilometers, China Earthquake Networks Center reported. The county has a population of 56,200, official statistics showed.

item.title: Xi urges drawing on Long March spirit
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-22
Xi urges drawing on Long March spirit He says inspiration of 'stirring heroic epic' provides wisdom and strength to forge ahead Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, called on Thursday for drawing strength from the Long March spirit to overcome difficulties, tackle risks and meet challenges, and to ensure that the giant ship of China's national rejuvenation cuts through the waves and sails steadily forward, as the country marked the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Red Army's Long March. Addressing a gathering at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, Xi linked the revolutionary journey nine decades ago to China's current pursuit of national rejuvenation, describing the drive to build China into a great modern socialist country in all respects, and to advance national rejuvenation on all fronts through Chinese modernization, as a new Long March for the Party and the people. Xi, who is also Chinese president and chairman of the Central Military Commission, said that revisiting history is about drawing wisdom and strength from it to forge ahead. He described the Long March, a strategic military maneuver carried out by the Workers' and Peasants' Red Army of the CPC from 1934 to 1936, as an earthshaking revolutionary feat of great significance in the history of the Party, the country and the military, with a profound impact on the path toward the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. "This stirring heroic epic will forever be engraved on the monument of the Chinese revolution and remembered in the hearts of hundreds of millions of people," he said. The Red Army traversed more than 10 provinces on a 12,500-kilometer journey and broke through encirclement and pursuit by more than a million enemy troops, opening up a new chapter in the Chinese revolution, Xi said. At his proposal, participants stood up and observed a moment of silence for the revolutionary heroes who gave their lives during the Long March and in revolutionary struggles across China. Reflecting on the path to the Long March victory, Xi highlighted the Party's correct leadership, firm revolutionary conviction, independence and a commitment to seeking truth from facts, as well as the support of the people. He emphasized the need to integrate the basic tenets of Marxism into China's specific realities, and to remain deeply rooted in the people, whom he described as the enduring source of strength and a strong support for the Party and the people's armed forces. The great spirit of the Long March, demonstrating the power of loyalty, truth, justice and unity, will always be a precious treasure and a powerful source of inspiration for overcoming difficulties and forging ahead, Xi said. Over the past 90 years, the Party has united and led the people through one great Long March after another during revolution, construction and reform, achieving one great victory after another, he said. Xi said the road of the Long March continues to extend. "On our new journey, we are now committed to realizing the second centenary goal of building China into a great modern socialist country in all respects and advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation on all fronts through a Chinese path to modernization," he said. Setting out the tasks ahead, Xi called for upholding the Party's ideals, convictions and fundamental purpose, remaining true to its original aspiration and founding mission, and relying closely on the people to make further historic achievements. He stressed the need to pursue high-quality development, better meet people's growing aspirations for a better life, and promote common prosperity for all. Economic development must deliver both improvements in quality and reasonable growth in quantity, he said. Xi also called for better coordination between development and security, and for taking the initiative to overcome difficulties, address risks and meet challenges. On national defense, he urged faster progress toward building world-class armed forces, upholding the Party's absolute leadership over the military, achieving the military's centenary goals on schedule, and advancing high-quality modernization of national defense and the armed forces. He further emphasized upholding Party leadership and strengthening Party building, with sustained efforts to exercise full and rigorous Party self-governance and enhance the Party's capacity to purify, improve and renew itself and excel.
